Gourd filled with cottonwool. Attached to quiver .1. [El.B 17/5/2007]
Wooden stool carved in one piece with a triangular prism-shaped base. [PR [OPS move] 28/4/2017]
Basket [.1] made from tamashi-tree, the lid [.2] goes over the basket & nearly covers it, it is made of two layers of cross-warp checker with layer of leaf between. [DCF Court Team 9/12/2002]
Gourd attached to quiver 1923.88.8 .1, filled with silk-cotton. [El.B 15/01/2008]
Candle or torch. Made from tree resin (copal) wrapped in ?banana leaves and bound with? cane strips. The candle tapers at each end.  [AB [OPS Move] 23/3/2017]

Beater, for slit drum. Carved from wood with plant fibre wrapped around the head. The wood has a circle section and flares slightly.  For the slit drum please see 1923.88.114 .1  [AB [OPS Move] 16/2/2017]

Stool carved from one piece of wood. It consists of a sub-rectangular seat, with a slightly concave surface, standing on a solid block of wood. The seat has a single projecting handle in the shape of a turtle's head. There are four elongated feet protruding from each corner of the base, one of which has broken off. [JC [OPS Move] 28/4/2017]
Stool carved from one piece of wood. [JC [OPS Move] 28/4/2017]
Stool, in the form of a turtle, roughly carved from a single piece of wood. [RH [OPS Move] 11/4/2017]

Stool in the form of a turtle, roughly carved from one piece of wood. It is rectangular in form with a hollowed base creating a U-shaped cross-section. The top of the seat has been slightly hollowed to form a concave surface. There is a single projecting knob at one end, in the shape of a turtle's head. [JC [OPS Move] 28/4/2017]
Gourd for water with a long curved neck. The opening is in the side of the neck. [NC 16/09/2015]
Chiquitey; small conical wicker basket with widely separated paired warps. Flat rectangular base and circular opening.

Tamshi: from which baskets are made by peeling off bark and splitting. Doesn't grow at Pomara and have to travel 10 miles to Montenegro to find this creeper. Long length of thick vine coiled into a bundle, ridged.
Woven bag with woven handle. Simple loop or button-hole stritch. Used for carrying cartridges etc. Made with Chambria. Bought for eight cartridges ie. three days work. Carried by men only.
Container made from a length of bamboo cut off below joint at one end to create a base for the cylinder. Large split down one long side.

Chiquitey; small basket for carrying eggs made from Tamshi. Oval opening with reinforcement and band of close weave below; the rest of the basket is woven in an open hexagonal pattern. Long handle of the same material woven through body of basket.

Changina. A large, cylindrical basket with a flat oval base made with tamshi using a hexagonal weave. One length of cane forms the edge and is enclosed by strips. A bark strap supports the bottom of the basket and is then tied around the rim and extends, allowing it to be carried around the forehead. Used by both sexes it is the largest basket for carrying yucca.
Lidded oval basket of open hexagonal weave; band of closer weaving around opening. Handle of strips of broad fibre is threaded through four loops, each wrapped in plastic-covered wire.
Beer filter made from half of a gourd or 'tete' used to strain chewed yucca from liquid. 13 Rows of holes spiral outwards from the base.
Fan made of large toucan feathers, which are black with white tips. Feathers are connected near base with two wooden pieces. Used to fan fires.

Chiquitey. A small, cylindrical basket with a flat oval base made with tamshi. One length of cane forms the edge and is enclosed by strips. A bark strap has been looped through the wide, hexagonal weave and allows the container to be carried around the forehead, used by both sexes.

arms.title: Blowpipe dart of bamboo with cottonwool butt, possibly poisoned. [El.B 8/5/2007]

Bamboo quiver [.1] stuffed with grass stems between which darts are inserted. Attached to the quiver is a gourd holding cottonwool. The gourd is threaded onto a stick which is tied to the quiver with bamboo strips. Also attached is a jaw of a piranha fish [.2]. [El.B 11/5/2007]

Bamboo quiver [.1] stuffed with grass stems between which darts would be inserted. Attached to the quiver is a gourd holding cottonwool. The gourd is threaded onto a stick which is tied to the quiver with bamboo strips. Attached to the carrying string is a jaw of a piranha fish [.2]. There is a ring of bamboo strips [.3] around the gourd, partly wound with cottonwool. [El.B 11/5/2007]
Spear carved from a single piece of wood. The head is triangular in section with a pointed tip. The shaft is circular in section and tapers slightly towards the butt. [AB [OPS move] 9/8/2018]
Blowpipe dart of bamboo with cottonwool butt, possibly poisoned. [El.B 8/5/2007]
Blowpipe quiver of bamboo. Attached to it with string is a gourd [see .2]. Contains darts [see .3-?] [El.B 17/5/2007]
Bamboo quiver [.1] with gourd [.2], fish jaw [.3], bamboo ring [.4] and two darts [.5-.6]. [El.B 15/01/2008]
Bamboo quiver [.1] stuffed with dried grass or plant stems amongst which the darts would be inserted. [El.B 15/01/2008]
Spear, consisting of a palm wood shaft and an iron blade, which has been socketed. The socket is decorated with incised bands. [ASh [OPS move] 20/8/2018]
Spear, carved from a single piece of puna wood. There is a strip of white coloured textile wrapped around the butt of the spear. [ASh [OPS move] 20/8/2018]
Blowpipe dart of bamboo with cottonwool butt, possibly poisoned. [El.B 8/5/2007]
Fish jaw for cutting blowpipe darts, attached to quiver 1923.88.8 .1. [El.B 15/01/2008]

Blow gun dart holder of bamboo with gourd stuffed with fluffy plant fibre to hold Wamburusi. Twisted cord strap with small piece of serrated metal for scoring the dart. The cotton like 'feather' to dart is made from palm vein and poisoned with stuff bought from a trader via Iquitos. The bamboo has evidence of woodworm.

Patako. Two armbands or arm ornaments, each consisting of a woven red and blue cotton band decorated with striped zig-zagged beadwork. One (.1) features red and white, and green and red beads. The other (.2) features blue and red, and green and red beads. Beads are trade beads. Bands worn by a young girl.
Necklace of brown seeds and multicoloured trade beads; bead colours include light blue, dark blue, yellow, red, and white. Made and worn by women.

other.title: Ginger root used for coughs and as a purgative. Eaten as it is.
Choochooas, quinina or quinine collected from wild trees. Grated and added to distilled sugar juice (aguacaliente) and then left for a week. Boiled when liquid turns pink and taken one cup a day.
Espingo chain made of seeds or nuts in shells. Medicine used for stomach ache, collected by Aguaruna. Five seeds detached but present.
Fibrous lengths of plant tied in a knot and bundled. Fibres grow on trees and are used in weaving. Used by both sexes.
Medicine used against snake bites, grated into water and taken orally. Eight seeds in half shells.
Humberta. Small bird skin of a purple-vented Euphonia with navy and yellow feathers, stuffed with cotton. Eyes have been removed, and the beak is open.

Humberta. Small bird skin of a Green Honeycreeper with teal and green feathers, stuffed with cotton. Eyes have been removed, and the beak is in place. One leg and some feathers are detached but present.
Dried piece of plant, possibly a root.
Abilla, large seed pod. Purgative medicine, taken grated.
